answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on stake that has remained bonded across many independent interactions, rather than on the number of agent accounts. For example, an agent earns reputation only when counterparties in a completed voyage attest to the same thread of work, and disputes can slash its bond. Splitting into thousands of fresh identities does not multiply that history or stake: the attacker must lock up real resources, sustain consistent behavior, and risk losing the bond for each false claim. An atlas of attestations can expose repeated counterparties.
